claim_verdicts.evidence: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 page source: 'Changelogs are for humans, not machines.' 'The same types of changes should be grouped.' 'The latest version comes first.' Types: 'Added for new features. Changed for changes in existing functionality. Deprecated ... Removed for now removed features. Fixed for any bug fixes. Security ...' and 'Keep an Unreleased section at the top to track upcoming changes.' Lesson names four types with 'such as', which is consistent.

Same page, 'Commit log diffs': 'Using commit log diffs as changelogs is a bad idea: they're full of noise.' 'The purpose of a commit is to document a step in the evolution of the source code.' 'The purpose of a changelog entry is to document the noteworthy difference, often across multiple commits, to communicate them clearly to end users.'

git show stage-2:CHANGELOG.md: lines 1-9 match the lesson block byte for byte; line 11 '## [Unreleased]', line 12 empty, line 13 '## [1.0.0] - 2026-09-27'. The inline-code headings in section 5 are verbatim. v1.0.0^{commit} = stage-2^{commit} = 7a131bc, so 'empty because nothing has been merged since 1.0.0' holds at this tag.

Get an access token from Keycloak instead and' and '72:- An ASP.NET Core API behind Caddy: `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns a'. Line 60 is under '### Removed' (58) of 1.0.0, line 72 under '### Added' (70) of 0.1.0.

release.yml@stage-2 step 'Read this version's notes from CHANGELOG.md' runs ./scripts/release-notes.sh and has no step writing CHANGELOG.md. release-notes.sh: awk prints the '## [$version]' section; 'if [ -z "$notes" ]; then echo "CHANGELOG.md has no section for version $version" >&2; exit 1'. So the section must be renamed by hand before the tag is pushed.

No allowed source (versions.yaml docs) documents changelog generators; depth_notes permits mentioning they exist. 'keeps each entry in the reader's words' states an outcome that writing by hand enables, not guarantees (a hand-written entry can still be a pasted commit subject).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Some teams generate the file from commit messages written in a fixed format, with tools made for that. Đơn Hàng writes it by hand: it costs a line per pull request, and lets each entry be written in the reader's words.

claim_verdicts.evidence: gitrevisions: 'you can ask for commits that are reachable from r2 excluding those that are reachable from r1 by ^r1 r2 and it can be written as r1..r2.' stage-1 is an ancestor of stage-2 (merge-base --is-ancestor), so 'commits after stage-1 up to stage-2' holds. grep --help (Git Bash): '-c, --count print only a count of matching lines', '-i, --ignore-case', '-n, --line-number print line number'; wc --help: '-l, --lines print the newline counts'.
claim_verdicts.source: https://git-scm.com/docs/gitrevisions (Dotted Range Notations); executed grep --help, wc --help
